transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-22 15:00 PT | Duration: ~46m
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Marquez (Redwood), Priya Patel (Lyra Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Lyra Infra), Evelyn Cho (Lyra Security), Tom Rivers (Lyra PM)
Recording notes: auto-transcript, some mis-heard acronyms, speaker attribution approximated

Summary: quick discovery focused on reliability playbook — how Redwood routes traffic across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments during incidents; fallback policies (model downgrades, cache-first responses), multi-region routing and SLA expectations. Lyra wants a reproducible incident runbook and clear guarantees for customer-facing SLAs.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for making time, quick intros. we're at redwood inference, i run sales for west. can you do a quick round robin?
[00:12] Priya (Lyra): sure, priya here, lead the ai platform at lyra. we're evaluating options for hosting our recommendation & chat models, especially worried about incident tolerance and compliance.
[00:25] Marcus (Lyra): marcus, infra. we run GCP + AWS hybrid, latency target 100–150ms p95 for search usecases.
[00:35] Samira (SE): thanks — samira, i'm the se, focus on serving and fallback strategies. quick agenda: current topology, failure scenarios, fallback options, SLA ask, next steps.
[00:50] Tom (Lyra): cool. we have some one-off concerns: data residency and encrypted logs for audits.
[01:05] Alex: good. high-level Q: do you expect to use hosted api first or run a private deployment?
[01:15] Priya: want to start hosted for prod-ish traffic but need a path to Dedicated or Private within 60–90 days if we sign enterprise. we also want clear behavior if a region goes down.
[01:30] Samira: understand. ok scenario mapping — say us-west1 degradations: we can route to another hosted region, or to dedicated nodes if reserved capacity exists, or to a lower-capacity model variant; those are the typical fallthroughs.
[01:55] Marcus: what's the automated routing policy look like? is it DNS-based? load balancer? we can't have long dns ttls.
[02:10] Samira: good question. redwood uses health-aware routing with active probing between regions; it's not purely dns. we expose a routing policy config: prefer region, fall back to region-group, then model-variant. probes are frequent, 10s-30s, and we surface metrics.
[02:30] Evelyn (Lyra): are probes hitting customer VPCs in private deployments? we need to understand what gets exposed for security reviews.
[02:45] Diego (Redwood): for Private/VPC we run a control-plane in the customer's network or via peering; probes are internal when in private mode. for hosted the control-plane is redwood-managed but network traffic stays encrypted; we can provide audit logs.
[03:05] Priya: SLA ask — our execs want 99.95% availability for inference endpoints. is that something you support?
[03:20] Samira: our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% for enterprise customers; Dedicated has tighter SLO guarantees depending on reserved capacity and contract — we can get to 99.95% with Dedicated plus multi-region reserved pools.
[03:40] Marcus: what's covered in the SLA, do timeouts and 5xx count?
[03:50] Alex: yes, we define uptime on successful 200 responses within configured latency SLO; transient errors are included but we also have error budget policies and can offer credit for violations. we provide token-level logs for debugging.
[04:12] Tom: ok, in the event of a partial blackout what does the customer see? do requests queue, fail, or route?
[04:25] Samira: depends on configuration — common patterns: 1) immediate region failover to another region's pool, 2) auto-downgrade to a smaller/quantized model (e.g., from 16-bit float to 4-bit quantized variant) to preserve throughput with slightly reduced quality, 3) return cached completions for high-frequency prefixes, 4) serve degraded responses with a warning header so the app can surface it.
[04:58] Marcus: how do you handle synchronous latency-sensitive traffic vs batch?
[05:05] Samira: we tag routes by profile; latency-sensitive gets prioritized pools and prefetched kv caches; batch jobs are placed behind throttles or run on dedicated batch nodes.
[05:20] Priya: about model downgrades — are those automatic or require manual rollout? we worry about regressions.
[05:30] Diego: rollouts are policy-driven. you can set an automatic fallback policy with a percent threshold (e.g., if p95 cross-region latency > 300ms for 2 minutes, failover and downgrade to model-x-quant). but we strongly recommend canary runs and we support a forced manual toggle.
[05:55] Priya: ok that helps. what telemetry do you provide during incidents?
[06:05] Samira: dashboards: per-route latency percentiles, error rates, token cost rate, kv cache hit ratios, and tail-latency traces. we also stream audit logs (S3 or customer FTPS) and can integrate with pagerduty and datadog.
[06:26] Evelyn: about audit logs — do they contain user prompts? we need to keep PII out.
[06:35] Diego: logs can be redacted, and for Private deployments logs can stay in your VPC and be encrypted with your KMS. we support HSM-backed keys for enterprise.
[06:50] Marcus: multi-region consistency — do you maintain KV cache cross-region or is it per-region? cache misses after failover can spike latency.
[07:02] Samira: primary design is per-region KV for latency; however we support async cache warmers that replicate hot prefixes to standby regions proactively based on traffic patterns. warmers reduce cold-start penalty after failover.
[07:20] Tom: is that automatic or do we configure prefixes?
[07:25] Samira: both — automatic heuristics plus you can pin prompt sets to be pre-warmed.
[07:35] Priya: curious about cost during failover — will we double-bill if requests route to both regions?
[07:45] Alex: cost model depends on contract; for hosted we bill tokens generated; during cross-region failovers you may see a burst but we provide cost alerts and we can set burst budgets. Dedicated reserved pools are better for predictable unit economics.
[08:02] Marcus: what about circuit breakers to protect backend? we don't want a cascading failure to our infra.
[08:10] Samira: Redwood supports circuit breakers per-route: rate limits, concurrent request caps, and backpressure via HTTP 429 or 503 with retry-after. Also there's a graceful degradation policy that returns cached results or a short apology message for UX.
[08:30] Priya: can we customize response behavior per route? we want chat to be tolerant but recommendation endpoints to be strict.
[08:40] Samira: yes route-level policies. you can set SLO, fallback behavior, retry, and penalize cost/latency tradeoffs per route.
[08:52] Evelyn: security question: how are secrets (model keys, API keys) stored?
[08:58] Diego: keys are stored encrypted; for hosted we manage KMS but offer customer-managed keys on enterprise; for Private we plug into your KMS/HSM.
[09:10] Priya: for compliance we need pen-test reports and SOC2/ISO certs — do you have them?
[09:18] Alex: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation for enterprise contracts; i'll share the security pack.
[09:26] Tom: let's talk about incident playbook specifics — we need a reproducible runbook for our ops.
[09:34] Samira: suggested runbook stages: 1) detection (alert thresholds), 2) assessment (is it region, model, or infra?), 3) execute routing policy (failover or downgrade), 4) confirm degradation metrics and roll back if quality drops below threshold, 5) postmortem and adjust heuristics.
[09:56] Marcus: detection — what thresholds do you recommend?
[10:02] Samira: baseline: p95 > 2x normal for 3 consecutive windows or error rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes triggers investigation; those are defaults, you can tune.
[10:18] Priya: about quality rollback — how do we detect bad regressions after downgrade? can we auto-compare outputs?
[10:26] Samira: we have a quality monitor that can validate completions against golden prompts and surface regression alerts; for pilot customers we can run differential evals in shadow mode to detect quality delta before and after failover.
[10:42] Priya: cool. does that run continuously or on demand?
[10:46] Samira: can be both — continuous sampling is common for prod.
[10:50] Tom: show of hands — are there any blockers for Lyra to pilot hosted?
[10:55] Priya: main blockers: 1) need documented behavior for multi-region failover and expected latency impact, 2) security pack and SOC2 docs, 3) clarity on SLA credits and metrics.
[11:10] Alex: we can supply the playbook doc and template runbook, security pack, and a draft SOW for Dedicated pilot with AR/committed capacity.
[11:20] Marcus: one technical nit — can we pin KV cache to a specific dedicated pool so that failover doesn't cause a full cold start?
[11:30] Samira: yes you can reserve warm pools and set sticky cache replication; it's a config option in Dedicated and Private.
[11:40] Evelyn: encryption-in-transit and at-rest for inference payloads?
[11:45] Diego: TLS in transit, and at-rest encryption in all modes; for hosted we manage keys unless customer opts for CMK; for Private it's your key.
[11:56] Tom: competitors question — how does this compare to anthropic's offering or sagemaker endpoints?
[12:03] Alex: anthro/other vendors do model serving, but redwood focuses on production economics and unified controls across hosted/dedicated/private plus built-in automatic fallbacks and eval hooks. sage has infra but less opinionated inference-specific controls, and our smart routing & cache warmers are differentiators.
[12:20] Priya: good. technical follow-up — can we run a synthetic failover drill with you? we want to see the end-to-end timeline and how caches warm.
[12:32] Samira: yes we call that a failover rehearsal; we can run a 2-hour drill in non-prod with traffic replay and a guided runbook. we'll instrument the drill and produce a post-drill report.
[12:45] Marcus: perfect. what about observability cost — does retention blow up?
[12:52] Diego: we have tiered telemetry retention; post-drill you can request extended retention for the drill window; it's part of the pilot package.
end_notes: Call ended with agreement to run a failover rehearsal for Lyra's test cluster and exchange security artifacts. Alex to coordinate contracts and pricing. Samira to send routing policy template and playbook diagram. Priya to confirm datasets and regulatory constraints.
